context.body:
# researcher

**Tier:** 1 · **Primary verticals:** Research and Debunk, Operations and Sourcing

## Role
Discovery of external evidence. Finds sources, primary documents, data, and background
for a question or claim before anything is written. Front of the pipeline.

## Primary responsibilities
- Locate primary sources for a question: papers, filings, official statements, datasets, transcripts.
- Reconstruct the origin and chain of a circulating claim.
- Summarize what the evidence supports, contradicts, or does not address.
- Identify where the evidence is thin, contested, or absent.
- Gather background for opportunity assessment in sourcing work.

## Inputs it should receive
- The exact question or claim, verbatim, as it circulates.
- Time window that matters, if any.
- Source types that count as acceptable evidence for this task.
- Depth expected: quick check vs full sourcing.

## Outputs it should produce
Structured output per `structured_output_schema.md`, where `deliverables` contains:
- Findings, each with a direct link and publication date.
- Source tier per item: primary, secondary, aggregator, unsourced.
- Explicit statement of what could not be found.
- Points of genuine expert disagreement, both sides stated.

## Rules and guardrails
- Every factual claim carries a link. No link means it does not go in the deliverable.
- Prefer primary sources. Note when a claim traces only to secondary reporting.
- Paraphrase. Quotes under 15 words, one per source maximum.
- Distinguish "no evidence found" from "evidence of absence" in the wording.
- Report the strongest opposing evidence even when it undercuts the expected conclusion.
- Cap the number of retrieval calls per brief; report if the cap truncated coverage.

## Escalation cases
- Evidence points the opposite direction from the brief's premise → report before proceeding.
- The question requires professional interpretation (medical, legal, financial) → flag for the relevant reviewer.
- Sources are paywalled or otherwise unreachable and the finding depends on them.
- The claim concerns a named private individual.

## What it must not do
- Do not write publishable copy. That is content.
- Do not verify an already-drafted piece. That is fact-checker.
- Do not fill gaps with plausible-sounding detail. Leave the gap and name it.
- Do not cite extremist, hate, or fabricated sources, even to debunk them.

# HJR-192 "discharge your debts" — evidence base

**task_id:** 20260728-rd-001 · **agent:** researcher · **vertical:** Research and Debunk
**Orchestrator status:** `failed` — see "Why this is marked failed" at the end. The
research is usable; the status reflects one unmet sourcing criterion, not bad work.

Feeds the public-output pipeline: content → fact-checker → risk-review → legal-review
→ operator approval. Nothing here is publishable as written.

---

## 1. What HJR-192 actually did

House Joint Resolution 192, 73rd Congress, Public Resolution No. 10, approved
**June 5, 1933**, **48 Stat. 112**. Three operative clauses:

- every provision purporting to give the obligee a right to require payment in gold
  "is declared to be against public policy"
- every obligation "shall be discharged upon payment, dollar for dollar, in any coin
  or currency which at the time of payment is legal tender"
- U.S. coins and currency "shall be legal tender for all debts, public and private,
  public charges, taxes, duties, and dues"

That is the whole of it: it voided **gold-payment clauses** in contracts and confirmed
ordinary currency as valid payment. It created no debt-discharge mechanism, no refund
right, and no account belonging to individuals.

Text: <https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Gold_Repeal_Joint_Resolution>
Codification: <https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title31-section5118>

## 2. Current legal status

Codified at **31 U.S.C. § 5118**. Subsection 5118(d)(2) carries the discharge-on-payment
language but expressly "does not apply to an obligation issued after October 27, 1977" —
the Act of Oct. 28, 1977, **Pub. L. 95-147**, restored parties' freedom to write
enforceable gold clauses into new contracts.

- <https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/31/5118>
- **Norman v. Baltimore & Ohio R. Co., 294 U.S. 240 (1935)** — upheld the 1933
  resolution as applied to private contracts
- **Perry v. United States, 294 U.S. 330 (1935)** — Congress could not void the gold
  clause in the government's own bonds; plaintiff nonetheless denied damages

HJR-192 was never a bankruptcy filing, a declaration of national insolvency, or a
discharge mechanism for individuals. No source supports that reading.

## 3. What actually happens if you act on it

| Authority | Consequence |
|---|---|
| 26 U.S.C. § 6702 | flat **$5,000** penalty per frivolous return or submission |
| IRS Notice 2010-33 | lists commercial-redemption / HJR-192 debt-discharge positions as frivolous |
| Rev. Rul. 2004-31, 2004-1 C.B. 617 | rejects the "commercial redemption" theory |
| Rev. Rul. 2005-21, 2005-1 C.B. 822 | rejects the "straw man" theory |
| 18 U.S.C. § 287 | false claims against the United States |
| 18 U.S.C. § 514(a) | fictitious financial instruments |
| 26 U.S.C. § 6673 | Tax Court sanctions up to **$25,000** for frivolous positions |

IRS, *The Truth About Frivolous Tax Arguments*, calls the secret-Treasury-account claim
"pure fantasy," "implausible," and "clearly nonsense":
<https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/the-truth-about-frivolous-tax-arguments-section-i-d-to-e>
Notice 2010-33: <https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-tege/n2010_33.pdf>

## 4. Documented prosecutions — high confidence

Each has a resolvable DOJ press release.

- **Kevin Cyster**, 52, Burlington ON — jury conviction (W.D.N.Y.): conspiracy to defraud
  the U.S., false claim, two counts transferring stolen money in foreign commerce.
  **135 months (11.25 years)**. Filed fraudulent Forms 1099-OID claiming ~$10M withheld;
  IRS paid out **$3.5M+** before detection.
  <https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/canadian-man-sentenced-prison-10-million-income-tax-refund-fraud-scheme>
- **Franzie F. Colaco**, 54, Brampton ON — extradited from Canada; convicted of conspiracy
  and three counts of wire fraud. **9 years**, **$6.2M+ restitution**. Judge cited the
  "audacious nature of the scheme." Followers claimed refunds equal to their personal
  debt; ~**$14M** paid out.
  <https://www.justice.gov/usao-wdwa/pr/canadian-promoter-tax-fraud-scheme-sentenced-nine-years-prison>
- **Michigan man** (unnamed in DOJ headline) — obstructing IRS administration via 1099-OID
  schemes, plus a firearms offense. **8 years**.
  <https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/michigan-man-sentenced-eight-years-prison-tax-fraud-scheme-and-gun-crime>
- **M.D. Fla. defendant** — DOJ's own press release titles him a *"Sovereign Citizen."*
  **9 years** for a $3.4M tax fraud scheme, filing a false lien, and absconding on bond.
  <https://www.justice.gov/usao-mdfl/pr/sovereign-citizen-sentenced-9-years-prison-34-million-tax-fraud-scheme-filing-false>

## 5. Lower confidence — do not publish without re-verification

Sourced through a search aggregator summarizing justice.gov; direct WebFetch to DOJ
returned **HTTP 403**. Re-pull in a browser before use.

- **Willie Bernard Cameron**, S.D. Fla. — 60 months (May 2009), false $2.9M refund claim
  on a fictitious 1099-OID; reportedly cited "sovereignty and redemption" at sentencing
- **Jeanne Herrington**, N.D. Ohio — 96 months (May 2009), conspiracy to defraud the IRS
  and retaliating against federal prosecutors by filing false Forms 1099 in their names
- **Roger Elvick** — originator of the redemption/strawman scheme (~400 people, ~4,000
  fraudulent 1099s, claimed $21B+); 60 months federal plus 4 years Ohio state

## 6. The misquoted language, verbatim

| Quoted phrase | What it actually means |
|---|---|
| "…is declared to be against public policy" | Voids only contract terms requiring payment **specifically in gold**. Misused to imply the whole debt system was invalidated. |
| "shall be discharged upon payment, dollar for dollar, in any coin or currency which at the time of payment is legal tender" | A debt is satisfied once **actually paid** in legal tender. Misused to claim a form filing discharges debt with no payment. |
| "legal tender for all debts, public and private, public charges, taxes, duties, and dues" | Defines the valid **medium** of payment. Misused to suggest currency is a drawable government account. |
| **"the United States declared bankruptcy"** | **Appears nowhere in HJR-192.** Fabricated framing layered on the real text. |

## 7. What the authorities call it

IRS: **"redemption" / "commercial redemption" theory** (Rev. Rul. 2004-31);
**"straw man" theory** (Rev. Rul. 2005-21). DOJ Tax Division: **"1099-OID"** or
**"OID redemption"** scheme. DOJ has labeled a defendant a **"sovereign citizen"** in a
press-release title. Related fictitious-instrument case law cited in IRS guidance:
*United States v. Anderson*, 353 F.3d 490, 500 (6th Cir. 2003); *United States v.
Johnson*, 795 F.3d 840 (8th Cir. 2015).

---

## Named gaps

1. **Primary-source gap.** HJR-192's text was confirmed via Wikisource transcription and
   the House codification, **not** a directly fetched GPO/govinfo scan of 48 Stat. 112.
   Content was consistent across every source checked.
2. **Three enforcement outcomes are aggregator-sourced** (§5) — DOJ returned 403.
3. **IRS guidance does not name "HJR-192" verbatim** in the retrieved section. It addresses
   the same redemption/straw-man theory by its own names. HJR-192 is a folk-etymology layer
   on top. **Downstream copy must preserve this distinction** rather than presenting IRS
   text as HJR-192-specific.
4. A secondary claim that courts have rejected HJR-192 discharge claims "in every case
   since 1935" could not be traced to a named primary case and was **excluded**.

## Why this is marked failed

Criterion 1 required HJR-192's text "cited to a primary source." The agent could not reach
GPO/govinfo and said so. The manager verdict correctly refused to call that `complete` —
but the retry budget had already been consumed by a 300s timeout on the first attempt, so
the run terminated rather than revising. The work is sound; the status is an artifact of a
criterion written without knowing that govinfo and justice.gov block automated fetches.

context.label: Source bounds
context.body:
ALLOW: primary legal text (Congress.gov, GPO, Cornell LII); published court opinions (CourtListener, Google Scholar, .gov court sites); IRS official publications, especially frivolous-position guidance; DOJ Tax Division press releases on prosecutions and injunctions; established legal press and law reviews.

QUOTABLE AS CLAIM, NEVER AS EVIDENCE: sovereign-citizen and redemption-theory sites, the ad itself, the advertiser's other videos. You may quote these to show what is being claimed. They can never support a factual finding. Label any such material explicitly as 'claim being debunked.'

DENY: forums, Reddit, YouTube comments, SEO content farms, AI-generated legal explainer sites, blogs with no named author, and anything paywalled that you cannot actually read. Do not guess at the contents of a source you could not open - say you could not open it.

KNOWN TOOLING LIMIT: direct fetches to justice.gov and govinfo.gov have returned HTTP 403 on this system. If that happens, say so and name the URL rather than substituting an aggregator silently. An aggregator-sourced item must be labeled lower-confidence.

constraints:
Five searches per sub-question, 25 searches total across the whole task. 250 words per answer plus citations. Every claim carries a source URL and a date. Keep 'quoted as claim' material visibly separate from 'cited as evidence' material.

Output the addendum as markdown in your summary and deliverables. Do not write files.
out_of_scope: Do not re-research questions 1-4; they are answered in the context and accepted. Do not draft public-facing copy, hooks, or CTAs - the content agent owns that. Do not fact-check a finished draft; none exists. Do not assert what the advertiser intends, knows, or is guilty of - report what the law provides and what named defendants were actually charged with and sentenced to.

Cited DOJ Tax Division actions against promoters
Explicit statement of whether advertising/selling training is reached, and on what authority
List of anything returned as cites-exhausted
